about.title: About
about.subtitle: Who I am
about.bio_1: 10 years in an industrial environment. Started with energy research on heating devices at ITPE Zabrze. Ended up writing software because I noticed most problems come from missing tools — not missing knowledge.
about.bio_2: I know hardware from both the electrical and code side. Neither side alone is usually enough.
about.bio_3: sincore is not a startup. It's a name under which I do concrete things for concrete people. If you have a problem that can be solved with software — write.
skills: Industrial systems and protocols (Modbus, RS-485, Siemens PLC)
Backend and integrations (Python, FastAPI, SQLite, REST)
Frontend and web applications (Next.js, TypeScript, React)
10 years of research in energy and industrial environments
about.approach: I understand the system before I write code. I don't sell solutions I know — I find solutions that work for the specific problem.
about.seo_description: Michał Pańczyk — ten years of energy and emissions research in a laboratory, now writing tools for problems I ran into myself.

services.title: Services
services.subtitle: What I fix. What I build.
services.cta_subtitle: Write two sentences about what's broken or what you need — we'll figure out the rest.
services.format_text: Every paid project comes with a Service Level Agreement (SLA) tailored to the engagement — service hours, response times, escalation rules. The template is available on request after our first conversation.
services.service_1_desc: An existing tool costs $150/month and has 80% of features you don't need? I build exactly what you need — once, flat fee, no subscription.
services.service_1_user: Small and medium-sized businesses for whom standard SaaS is too expensive, doesn't fit, or doesn't cover the specifics of their process. Owners of 5-50 person companies, operations managers, lab managers.
service_1_value: Lower total cost than a yearly SaaS subscription for 10+ seats
Functionality fitted to the process, not the other way around
No vendor lock-in — code, data and infrastructure stay with the client
service_1_includes: Deployment on client infrastructure or Vercel
service_1_excludes: Data migration from legacy systems (separate project)
services.service_2_desc: Reports made manually, data copied between systems, repetitive tasks eating hours every week. It can be automated.
services.service_2_user: Companies with existing systems (ERP, CRM, lab equipment, PLC controllers), where manual data shuffling or a missing connection costs daily employee time.
service_2_value: Custom integrations for non-standard protocols (Modbus, RS-485, OPC UA, custom APIs)
No monthly task limits typical of iPaaS platforms
service_2_includes: Map of existing systems and identification of manual touchpoints
Integration design (transport, data mapping, error handling, monitoring)
Implementation (Python, Java, Node — chosen per case)
services.service_3_desc: Hardware works but no software to operate it? I write applications communicating via Modbus, RS-485, COM port — from data reading to control.
services.service_3_user: Laboratories, R&D departments, manufacturing companies with industrial equipment. Lab managers, auditors, automation engineers — where the manufacturer shipped the device but the data-logging software is archaic, missing, or doesn't fit the procedure.
service_3_value: Measurement capture aligned with lab procedures (timestamp, operator, CSV/XLSX export)
Device configuration from PC without physical panel access
Protocol-level fault detection (loose thermocouple, frame error) — alarms before bad data reaches the report
service_3_includes: Protocol analysis if the manufacturer doesn't publish documentation
services.service_4_desc: Orders in Excel, statuses in the boss's head, reports made on Fridays. I build simple systems for order management, status tracking and reporting — without a corporate ERP.
services.service_4_user: Micro and small businesses (up to about 20 people), freelancers with a team, sole proprietors outsourcing some work. Where a full ERP/CRM is overkill, but Excel and an inbox are not enough.
service_4_value: One screen, one purpose — fast input and status check
Recurring reports generated without manual work
Hosted on client infrastructure or ours
service_4_includes: Discovery (one process — orders, statuses or reports)
Design and implementation as a web application
service_4_excludes: Accounting and invoicing integrations (separately under Process automation)
services.service_5_desc: Free tools for technicians and engineers — ready to download from the site, no login, no subscription, no telemetry. Producer marked as sincore.io in the file metadata.
services.service_5_user: The industry community: technicians, automation engineers, lab managers working with industrial equipment, who need a working tool without cost or paperwork.
service_5_value: Working tool ready to use immediately (Waga, MB-TC)
sincore.io signature in metadata — brand identifier in the technical environment
service_5_includes: README and documentation in the GitHub repo
New versions released every few months
service_5_excludes: Email/phone one-on-one support (that's already Industrial systems)
Guarantee of operation on unusual hardware configurations
services.seo_description: What I fix and what I build: automating repetitive work, reading data out of instruments, industrial protocol integrations.
